subject: sentences
title: Yesterday, now, tomorrow
about: He picks the verb that fits the time word: yesterday I washed, right now the frog hops, tomorrow we will walk. NC's K-1 grammar continuum asks that verbs convey a sense of time, and CKLA teaches past and present tense in Unit 3 and past, present and future in Unit 4.
tip: Point at the time word first (yesterday, right now, tomorrow) and ask whether it already happened, is happening, or has not happened yet.

cards.sayQ: Yesterday I, blank, the dishes. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Yesterday means it already happened, so the verb ends in ed.

cards.sayQ: Last night Dad, blank, a cake. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Last night means it already happened, so the verb ends in ed.

cards.sayQ: Yesterday we, blank, in the park. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Yesterday means it already happened, so the verb ends in ed.

cards.sayQ: Last week Pam, blank, a seed. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Last week means it already happened, so the verb ends in ed.

cards.sayQ: Right now the frog, blank. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Right now means it is happening.

cards.q: Right now the dog ___ at the cat.
cards.sayQ: Right now the dog, blank, at the cat. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Right now means it is happening.

cards.sayQ: Right now Kim, blank, her hands. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Right now means it is happening.

cards.sayQ: Tomorrow we, blank, to the zoo. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Tomorrow has not happened yet, so we say will.

cards.sayQ: Next week we, blank, the fish. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Next week has not happened yet, so we say will.

cards.sayQ: Tomorrow Beth, blank, a kite. Which word fits the blank?
cards.note: Tomorrow has not happened yet, so we say will.
